context: Daichi takes Sho-young to a small post office to mail birthday card.
purpose: Father teaching child practical postal task.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Dad, do I put the stamp here?
lines.style: Soft, hesitant question. Seeks reassurance rather than information. Warm and focused—watching his father's face for approval. Small, genuine curiosity.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: Yeah, go ahead and stick it right there.
lines.style: Encouragement wrapped in warmth. Kansai lilt on the ending. Relaxed and present—the voice of a father who knows this moment matters to his son.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Is the envelope okay like this?
lines.style: Checking again—not from doubt but from wanting to do it right. Quiet, careful attention. The slight uptick at the end waits for confirmation.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: Affirmation that lands. Kansai warmth on the second word. Genuine pride—not over-performing, just delighted his son got it exactly right.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おばあちゃんに、届くね!
lines.style: Brightness breaks through—small wonder at the magic of mail. Soft excitement, no performance. The joy of understanding something real is about to happen.
